stem_book: [One or more options may be correct] Choose the incorrect statement(s) among the following: (a) The entropy of water increases from 0° to 4°C (b) The change in entropy of 3 moles of an ideal monoatomic gas by doubling the temperature (K) at constant pressure is nearly 43.2 J K⁻¹ (c) For the free expansion of a gas in an isolated system the internal energy remains constant (d) The work done by a real gas in an isothermal reversible expansion is greater than that of an ideal gas
reason: Printed key 'ad' calls (a) incorrect, but heating water 0→4°C at constant P absorbs heat, dS = C_p dT/T > 0 — entropy rises despite the density anomaly; only (d) is incorrect.
work: (a) ΔS = C_p ln(277/273) > 0 true; (b) 3·(5/2)·8.314·ln2 = 43.2 true; (c) q = w = 0 ⇒ ΔU = 0 true; (d) attractions make P_real < P_ideal ⇒ less work — false
